limitations: This document pools the six reporting windows into a single analysis: March-November 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, plus March-July 2026. Months outside those windows - December, January and February, and August 2026 - are excluded, so this is the six periods analysed together rather than everything ever collected.

Complaints by period: 2021 28, 2022 66, 2023 56, 2024 70, 2025 92, 2026 191. Volume rises steeply toward the present, so recent years carry this pooled ranking. For a like-for-like comparison across years, use the six period reports, where each period is normalised to its own share.

Because every window runs March to November, winter is absent by construction. Snow, flooding and storm response therefore sits near the bottom here; in a pool that included December through February it ranks first. Neither figure is wrong - they answer different questions.
Coverage is uneven across the span. Instagram's public feed could not be paged back past March 2023, so the 2021 and 2022 windows are Facebook-only, while later windows draw on both platforms.
Facebook history was gathered as date-bounded slices rather than an exhaustive crawl, so each window is a sample of that period rather than every post the city published in it.

Facebook comments were pulled from the most-commented posts in each window. Heavily discussed posts are over-represented on purpose - that is where grievances collect - so these shares describe the complaint conversation, not the average post.
Instagram contributes the comments returned alongside each post, a broader but shallower slice than Facebook.
Emoji-only, tag-only and one-word reactions are counted in the total collected but excluded from the base used for the complaint rate, since they express no grievance either way.
Comments posted by official city accounts are excluded, as the scrapers surface them alongside residents' replies.
A category can rank low simply because the city rarely posted about it. Treat the ranking as a measure of the conversation the city's own posts invited, not a census of civic opinion.
